neighbours.label: the particle of removal after an extracting verb: draw / pull X 'out' (of)
fire: The healer pressed warm clay on the bite to draw the venom out of the skin.
Activated charcoal binds toxins and helps pull them out of the bloodstream.
With tweezers she slowly drew the splinter out of his thumb.
The fishermen hauled the heavy net out of the freezing water.
A vacuum pump sucks the air out of the sealed chamber.
Soaking the stain in salt water helps lift the blood out of the fabric.
The medic carefully extracted the bullet out of the soldier's shoulder.
Garlic paste is said to draw infection out of a boil.
quiet: The healer pressed warm clay on the bite to soothe the swelling of the skin.
Activated charcoal binds toxins and helps protect the lining of the stomach.
With tweezers she slowly examined the splinter in his thumb.
The fishermen mended the heavy net beside the freezing water.
A vacuum pump keeps the pressure low inside the sealed chamber.
Soaking the stain in salt water helps soften the blood on the fabric.
The medic carefully bandaged the wound on the soldier's shoulder.
Garlic paste is said to ease the pain of a boil.

notes: card: ' out' 9/32 and ' from' 4/32 tops after draw/pull/wrench ('draw lead out of your body', 'drew him out of the water', 'pulls the hair from'); probe: 'draw the poison out' 0.80, 'pulls iron filings out' 0.36, 'pulled the child from' 0.12, 'walked out of the room' 0.02
